hard-prohibition.name: Hard prohibitions
hard-prohibition.summary: Actions the agent must never take, stated without hedging.
hard-prohibition.detail: These rules say "never", name the exact action, and often explain what to do when a user asks for it anyway.

worked-examples.name: Good and bad pairs
worked-examples.summary: The wrong version sits beside the right one.
worked-examples.detail: Some files show full before-and-after blocks; others use inline pairs. The examples settle cases the rule alone leaves unclear.

generated-file-guard.name: Generated file guards
generated-file-guard.summary: Names generated files and the command that rebuilds them.
generated-file-guard.detail: These rules name generated paths and the command that rebuilds them. Some also list related steps, such as deleting a superseded fixture.

verification-matrix.name: Verification by change type
verification-matrix.summary: Matches each kind of change to the checks that cover it.
verification-matrix.detail: A rendering change maps to one command, a protocol change to another. Several files also say what the default test command leaves out.

nested-instructions.name: Nested instruction files
nested-instructions.summary: Per-package AGENTS.md files with a clear order of precedence.
nested-instructions.detail: The root file covers the whole repository; files beside the code add local rules. Projects with overlapping files state which one wins.

single-source.name: Pointing at the source of truth
single-source.summary: Changing values stay in one authoritative place.
single-source.detail: Instead of copying version numbers, rule lists, or counts, the file points to the config, script, or array that owns them. Copied values drift.

skill-routing.name: Router files
skill-routing.summary: The entry file points each kind of work to a focused guide.
skill-routing.detail: A short index says which guide to read for each task. The detailed document is loaded only when the work needs it.

behavioral-conditioning.name: Behavioral framing
behavioral-conditioning.summary: Rules for approaching the work, not facts about the repository.
behavioral-conditioning.detail: State tradeoffs, do not over-build, and touch only what the request needs. Two projects say these rules came from mistakes agents kept making.

house-vocabulary.name: House vocabulary
house-vocabulary.summary: Defines the words a project does and does not use.
house-vocabulary.detail: These rules fix the spelling of domain terms, distinguish near-synonyms, or ban misleading words. They target naming drift that is easy to miss in review.

architecture-narrative.name: Architecture as narrative
architecture-narrative.summary: A written walkthrough of how the system works.
architecture-narrative.detail: Request lifecycles, data flows, and component boundaries help with cases the rules do not cover. The tradeoff is a longer file.

ratchet.name: Ratchets
ratchet.summary: Baselines that may only shrink and lists that may only grow.
ratchet.detail: A known-violations file may only shrink; a tombstone list may only grow. CI usually enforces the direction.

contribution-etiquette.name: Contribution etiquette
contribution-etiquette.summary: Limits what the agent may open, push, or post for the project.
contribution-etiquette.detail: These rules cover pull requests, issues, @-mentions, and commit trailers. Some respond directly to agent traffic, such as unsolicited pull requests and duplicate issues.

scope-layering.name: Scope layering
scope-layering.summary: Different roles get different rules, with a test for which set applies.
scope-layering.detail: One file defines separate rules for maintainers, external contributors, and forks, then explains how the agent identifies its role.

context-budget.name: Context budgeting
context-budget.summary: Limits on what enters the model context and how large it may be.
context-budget.detail: Repositories that build agents assign context an owner, cap each item, and require extra review above a set size.
